analysis.title: GS Armbrust - What Matters Today: Largest Drop in Gross leverage since Covid and biggest in net since Liberation day, CTAs are Large Sellers of US Equities, Watch US Panic Index and Multiple Surprise Ratio, GIR Says Semis are Oversold (9 Nov 2026)
key_insights: US equities were modestly net sold last week, driven by the largest single stock net selling in 4 months, partly offset by buying in Macro Products.

Info Tech was by far the most net sold global and US sector in dollar terms. The week's percentage selling in global Info Tech stocks was about equal to the largest net selling weeks on GS record (since 2016). 4 of the top 5 such weeks have occurred in the past five months.

US Fundamental L/S gross leverage fell 8.7 pts to 207.5% (26th percentile one-year), the largest weekly decline since March 2020. Net leverage fell 3.7 pts to 43.3% (0th percentile five-year), the largest weekly decline since Liberation Day (Apr 2025). Armbrust reads this as a strong signal that positioning is cleaning up.
Fundamental L/S returned -1.48% last week, with US Fundamental L/S down almost 2% and Systematic L/S down 0.6%.
GS's proprietary risk appetite index continues to fall sharply. A reading of -1 is a strong buy signal and -1.5 is a stronger one, but it is not at clear buying levels yet.
Systematic/CTA signals are negative in about 60% of global equity markets at short and medium-term trend horizons, including the S&P 500 and most of the largest markets.
GS expects CTAs to sell $28bn of SPX futures over the next week and $45bn over the next month in the baseline scenario, which would take the position to net short.
The US Panic Index hit 9.57 on Thursday and closed the week at 9.2. Readings above 9 have historically been a good buying opportunity.

The multiple surprise ratio (a day's % move relative to 1-month implied vol) for SPX was the largest in 19 years this week. NDX ranked top 2 and RTY top 5. Armbrust says the vol market underpriced the move.
GS Research (GIR) says stocks are clearly oversold. It sees few catalysts before year end but compelling risk/reward in select names.

market_movers.rationale: GIR favors NVDA in AI Compute because the stock implies no growth from 2027.
GIR favors AVGO in AI Compute because the stock implies no growth from 2027.
GIR prefers AMAT in semi cap equipment, treating 2027 wafer fab equipment spending as a baseline.
GIR prefers LRCX in semi cap equipment, treating 2027 wafer fab equipment spending as a baseline.

sector_views.rationale: GIR says semis are oversold with compelling risk/reward in select names, though catalysts before year end may be few.
GIR sees 2027 WFE as a baseline and prefers AMAT and LRCX.
GIR says memory is approaching oversold levels as it moves toward tangible book.

risk_factors: GIR sees few catalysts for stocks to rise before year end.
CTA selling could continue and push the systematic position to net short.
Risk appetite is low but not yet at the -1 reading GS treats as a strong buy signal.
vol_and_positioning: US Fundamental L/S gross leverage is 207.5% (26th percentile one-year) after an 8.7 pt weekly drop, the largest since March 2020.
US Fundamental L/S net leverage is 43.3% (0th percentile five-year) after a 3.7 pt weekly drop, the largest since April 2025.
CTA signals are negative in about 60% of global equity markets. GS expects $28bn of SPX futures selling over 1 week and $45bn over 1 month in the baseline, taking the position to net short.

US Panic Index (equal-weighted basket of percentile ranks of VIX, SPX skew, SPX term structure and SPX 1-month at-the-money implied vol) peaked at 9.57 Thursday and closed at 9.2. Readings above 9 have historically marked buying opportunities.
SPX had the largest multiple surprise ratio in 19 years, NDX was top 2 and RTY top 5.
